text_blocks.snippet: A patient with a severe systemic disease has a significant health condition that affects multiple organ systems and causes substantial limitations in their ability to function normally. This classification, often designated as ASA III (American Society of Anesthesiologists), indicates a patient whose disease poses a threat to their overall well-being and may impact their response to medical treatment or surgery.
snippet_highlighted_words: has a significant health condition that affects multiple organ systems and causes substantial limitations in their ability to function normally

text_blocks.snippet: The ASA physical status classification system is a way to assess a patient's overall health and fitness before surgery or other medical procedures. It's used by anesthesiologists to determine the level of risk associated with administering anesthesia and performing the procedure.

An ASA III patient has a severe systemic disease that is not immediately life-threatening but significantly limits their daily activities and functional capacity. Examples of conditions that might place a patient in this category include:

list.snippet: Moderate reduction of ejection fraction (heart's pumping ability).
History of myocardial infarction (heart attack) or stroke more than 3 months prior.

text_blocks.snippet: Patients with severe systemic disease may require:

list.title: More careful monitoring during procedures:
list.snippet: Anesthesiologists need to be aware of the patient's limitations and adjust anesthesia accordingly.

list.title: Specialized care and management:
list.snippet: Depending on the specific condition, additional interventions or medications may be necessary.

list.title: Potential for complications:
list.snippet: The presence of severe systemic disease can increase the risk of complications during or after treatment.

text_blocks.snippet: In summary, a patient with severe systemic disease (ASA III) is someone whose overall health is significantly impacted by a chronic condition, requiring careful consideration and management during medical interventions.
